status.en: 20 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 44% fewer than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 20 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 44 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Ethiopian forces have moved into the strategic Tigray towns of Adwa and Adigrat, both close to the Eritrean border, while pro-government militia say they have taken the regional airport. Ethiopian drones have struck Eritrean troops that crossed into Ethiopian territory to support Tigrayan rebels. Both sides have appealed to the UN for deterrence or intervention, with Ethiopia framing its actions as self-defence against Eritrean incursions. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopiske styrker har rykket inn i de strategiske Tigray-byene Adwa og Adigrat, begge nær grensen til Eritrea, mens pro-regjeringsmilitsen sier de har tatt regionalflyplassen. Etiopiske droner har angrepet eritreiske tropper som krysset inn i etiopisk territorium for å støtte tigrayanske opprørere. Begge sider har henvendt seg til FN for avskrekking eller intervensjon, der Etiopia fremstiller handlingene som selvforsvar mot eritreiske inntrengninger. Konflikten forårsaket 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
